title: Geometric-fibre admissibility and the semilinear Frobenius inverse
statement: Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and let $a_X:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the second projection. Let $\gamma$ and $\varphi_q=\gamma^{-1}$ be geometric and arithmetic Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Then $a_X$ is separated and of finite type, $X$ is Noetherian, and there is $d\in\mathbf N$ with $\dim X\le d$ (with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$). Here Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth], and dimension is Krull dimension [def-kun-dimension]. For every $x\in X$, the element $\ell\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a unit, with inverse the image of $\ell^{-1}\in k$ under $k\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The morphism $g_X=\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ is an automorphism of schemes with inverse $\operatorname{id}_{X_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi_q)$. These assertions require neither finiteness of the field extension $k/k_0$, nonemptiness of $X$, nor $k$-linearity of $g_X$.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], $a_X$ is the base change of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Apply [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] to this square. Thus $a_X$ is separated and of finite type; this theorem allows an arbitrary base morphism, so no finite-extension hypothesis is used.

Every ideal of the field $k$ is $(0)$ or $(1)$, so $k$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. The single affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; its one-point space is quasi-compact. Hence the Noetherian-target hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] holds for $a_X$. Together with step 1 this gives that $X$ is locally Noetherian and quasi-compact, as required.

Apply [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], recorded as AlgebraicGeometry.exists_topologicalKrullDim_le, to the geometric-fibre structure morphism with K=k and the finite-type hypotheses of step 1. Its conclusion is exactly the required natural-number bound on the dimension [def-kun-dimension]; it includes the empty fibre without any nonemptiness hypothesis.

proof.text: The cardinality in [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] gives characteristic p on k_0 by charP_of_card_eq_prime_pow, implementing [def-weil-finite-field-q-elements]. Injectivity of the algebra map transfers this characteristic to k. CharP.cast_ne_zero_of_ne_of_prime shows that the prime ell distinct from p is nonzero in k. At each point x, form the unit Units.mk0 ell and map it through the specified composite k -> Gamma(X,O_X) -> O_{X,x}. The ring homomorphism preserves natural-number casts, so its value is ell, and Units.map sends the inverse to the image of ell^{-1}, definitionally. The assertion is vacuous if X is empty.

proof.text: Use the two inverse identities hom_inv_id and inv_hom_id of the already constructed geometricFrobenius automorphism [def-weil-frobenius-detailed]. Its stored inverse is the galoisMap of the inverse geometric field Frobenius. FiniteField.geometricFrobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_eq_inv, AlgEquiv.aut_inv and AlgEquiv.symm_symm identify this coefficient automorphism with arithmetic Frobenius. These yield exactly the two displayed identities, without any Cartesian-square theorem or k-linearity assumption.
